# pbs_datastore_s3_refresh (Action)

Refreshes a Proxmox Backup Server datastore on S3 from its bucket, as **Refresh contents from S3 bucket** under the datastore's Content → More in the web interface does: PBS reads the namespaces, groups and backup indexes the bucket holds under the datastore's name into the datastore's local cache, in place of those the cache had. The chunks stay in the bucket. That brings the cache back in line with the bucket, such as after the stray objects of a failed backup were removed from the bucket by hand, which PBS recommends when the object store ran out of space, or after files of the cache were lost or damaged. A datastore created with `reuse_datastore`, such as to take over the datastore of a PBS that is gone for good, is refreshed as part of its creation.

~> One datastore, one PBS: never have two PBS use the same datastore — the same bucket under the same name — not even for a test. Each one's garbage collection deletes from the bucket the chunks that only the other's backups use, and a refresh does not prevent that. To have the backups on a second PBS, sync them to a datastore of its own.

Needs `Datastore.Modify` on the datastore, and `Datastore.Audit` to read its configuration first; the `DatastoreAdmin` role has both. The action refuses a datastore that is not on S3 before asking PBS, which would leave such a datastore in maintenance mode `s3-refresh`. Every PBS 4 release can refresh a datastore.

~> PBS puts the datastore into maintenance mode `s3-refresh` for the refresh, replacing any mode it had, such as `read-only`: no backup, restore, prune or garbage collection passes until it is done. PBS 4.0.20 and later first wait for the operations that use the datastore to end, without limit, and then hold the lock of the datastore configuration while they read, which holds up the other datastores of the server too: operations that open one, and changes to the settings of any, wait for it for 10 seconds, then fail. A refresh that succeeds clears the maintenance mode; it does not restore an earlier one, which the next apply of a `pbs_datastore` that configures `maintenance_mode` sets again.

A refresh that fails leaves the datastore in maintenance mode `s3-refresh`, and the action then says so: fix the cause and invoke the action again, or clear the mode under Datastore → Options → Maintenance Mode in the web interface, or with `proxmox-backup-manager datastore update <store> --delete maintenance-mode` on the host. `pbs_datastore` does not replace a maintenance mode PBS set itself: while the datastore is in `s3-refresh`, it keeps the configured `maintenance_mode` in state and warns when it reads the datastore.

When the wait ends first, the refresh goes on in PBS, which clears the maintenance mode when it is done. PBS logs a line per object it reads; the action reports the latest every few seconds.

-> Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later. OpenTofu and older Terraform releases do not support them, and Terraform 1.13 ignores `action` blocks without a word; set `required_version = ">= 1.14.1"` in configurations that use them. An action runs when a resource's `lifecycle` `action_trigger` fires, or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.<type>.<name>`, which also refreshes the state of the resources the action's configuration refers to, and of those they depend on, but of no other resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  # Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later; Terraform 1.13 would ignore them.
  required_version = ">= 1.14.1"
}

# The datastore s3store1 of the pbs_datastore example, on S3, assumed in the
# same configuration. When its bucket ran out of space during a backup, PBS
# could not clean up after it: remove that backup's stray objects from the
# bucket by hand, as PBS recommends, then set var.bucket_cleanup to the day,
# which refreshes the datastore so that its local cache matches the bucket
# again. Or refresh it yourself:
# terraform apply -invoke=action.pbs_datastore_s3_refresh.s3store1
#
# One datastore, one PBS: never have a second PBS use this datastore, the
# same bucket under the same name, not even for a test. Each one's garbage
# collection deletes the chunks that only the other's backups use, and a
# refresh does not prevent that. To have the backups on a second PBS, sync
# them.
resource "terraform_data" "bucket_cleanup" {
  input = var.bucket_cleanup

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_update]
      actions = [action.pbs_datastore_s3_refresh.s3store1]
    }
  }
}

# No backup or restore passes the datastore while PBS refreshes it.
action "pbs_datastore_s3_refresh" "s3store1" {
  config {
    store   = pbs_datastore.s3store1.name
    timeout = "1h"
  }
}

variable "bucket_cleanup" {
  description = "Day stray objects were last removed from the bucket by hand, such as 2026-11-14."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `store` (String) Name of the datastore on S3, such as `pbs_datastore.s3.name`.

### Optional

- `timeout` (String) How long to wait for the PBS task, as a Go duration such as `90m` or `4h`. Defaults to the provider's `task_timeout`. When it runs out, the action fails, and the task goes on in PBS.
- `wait` (Boolean) Whether to wait for the PBS task to finish. Defaults to `true`: the action reports the task's progress, and fails when the task fails. With `false`, the action ends as soon as PBS has started the task, and the task's outcome is only in PBS (Administration → Tasks).
